identity_notes: Most human efficacy evidence concerns oral apple cider vinegar (ACV) at approximately 15-30 mL/day for glycemic/lipid/weight outcomes, generally showing small, heterogeneous benefits on fasting glucose, HbA1c, and anthropometrics but consistently null results on insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and LDL/HDL across multiple systematic reviews. The single most important applicability caveat: one of the larger positive weight-management RCTs in this set (PMID 38966098, 120 participants) was subsequently RETRACTED (PMID 41789013) and should not be relied upon; some pooled meta-analyses in this set may have been published before the retraction and could include that study's data. Separately, a recurring safety theme across case reports is local/topical tissue injury (esophageal injury from tablets, dental erosion from daily undiluted consumption, chemical skin burns from topical use) and rare systemic adverse events (hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, and a hypokalemia/hyperreninemia/osteoporosis case from very large intake), consistent with ACV's acidity and typically undiluted/high-volume misuse patterns rather than at standard studied doses.
